top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, KLOwen, damon ultima brackets, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, Lightforce, SmartSTL, SLB, self-ligating braces
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, rentability, time saving, visit reduction, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, staff efficiency, practice optimisation, emergencies reduction, dynamic scheduling, average visit reduction, efficiency in bracket systems, bonding failures, door breakage, performance in NHS Hospital environment, efficiency in second and third order movements
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually save time or money, or that it will meaningfully reduce appointments or chair time. Some believe the workflow changes are not worth the investment, or that the benefits are only for aligners, not braces. Others want proof of ROI or are concerned about increased workload or costs.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Evidence that DM reduces number of visits for braces cases
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
Resources that explore the benefits of self-ligating bracket monitoring and using insights with braces
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for robust, region-specific ROI and efficiency data, especially for braces and mixed appliance practices. More real-world, peer-reviewed studies quantifying time and cost savings in diverse practice settings would be valuable.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI and SmartSTL for clinical monitoring and diagnostics
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of SmartSTL, comparison to intraoral scan, FDA class I, occlusal assessment, accuracy in detecting malocclusions, accuracy of scanning, AI versus orthodontist, AI algorithm, predictability parameters, accuracy class I goal
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI is as accurate as a human orthodontist, especially for clinical observations and diagnostics. Some do not trust AI or SmartSTL, fearing errors or misdiagnosis, and want proof of reliability and regulatory validation.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, white paper, peer-reviewed, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
top_needs.gap_assessment: More head-to-head studies comparing AI/SmartSTL to human experts and intraoral scans, especially in real-world clinical settings, are needed. Regulatory validation and detailed accuracy metrics for specific clinical tasks should be prioritized.
